# Contract field reference, schema 0.7.7 preview

Status: **preview**. A contract opts in with `fluidVersion: "0.7.7"`; a contract that declares 0.7.6 is unaffected. This page lists the difference between the 0.7.6 schema and the 0.7.7 schema as bundled with the CLI: added fields, fields whose definition changed, and fields removed. A field not listed here has the same type, required flag, allowed values, default and description in both; for those, use the [0.7.6 reference](./contract-0.7.6.md). A definition used at several paths is listed once, at its first path.

Generated from `fluid_build/schemas/fluid-schema-0.7.7.json` in the `data-product-forge` 0.29.0 package (sha256 `0f11fb44bc9dafbc`). It is the schema `fluid validate` checks a contract against, rendered without edits. To regenerate: `python scripts/gen_contract_reference.py`.

Each table row is one field, addressed by its path from the contract root: `.` descends into an object, `[]` marks the items of a list, and `<key>` stands for any key of a map. **Required** means required inside its parent object; the parent can itself be optional. **Allowed values** lists the enum, pattern and range the schema enforces. An object typed plainly `object` rejects keys the schema does not list; `object (open)` accepts extra keys and `object (free-form)` has no listed keys. A row that begins "Only when ..." exists only under that condition. See [how to read this reference](./README.md#how-to-read-a-row).

## At a glance

- Added: 142 rows
- Changed: 2 rows
- Removed: 0 rows

| `builds[].properties.stream` | object | no |  |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.7 (preview): The stream the build reads. On a managed Flink build (parameters.flink.management) sql is optional: the lane writes the query from the mapping instead. Elsewhere the stream describes what the build's own sql reads. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.kind` | string | yes | must be `kafka` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. The streaming system. Only kafka in this preview. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.topic` | string | yes | matches `^(?!\.\.?(?![\s\S]))[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,249}(?![\s\S])` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. One Kafka topic, by name: Kafka's legal characters (not . or ..), no pattern and no list. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.format` | string | yes | one of `json`, `avro-confluent` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. How record values are encoded. json: one JSON object per record; a field the schema does not declare is ignored, and a declared field that is missing reads as null. avro-confluent: Avro in the Confluent Schema Registry wire format. The declared schema is the reader schema, so the producers' subject must stay readable by it: FORWARD or FULL compatibility, transitive. |

| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality` | array of object | no | each item: min properties 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.6: Column-level data quality rules, in ODCS's own shape — the array that is written straight into `schema[].properties[].quality[]` of the exported ODCS v3.1.0 contract, and the array an imported ODCS column's rules are read back into, inline on the column rather than in the importer's pass-through bucket: the ODPS importer merges a resolved port's `contract` block into its output-port stub and discards the sub-import's root `extensions`, so rules left in that bucket were dropped outright by a FLUID → ODPS → FLUID cycle. The ODCS exporter has always replayed this key verbatim and always read it back on import, but `$defs.column` is `additionalProperties: false` and did not define it, so a column written the way the exporter supports was REFUSED by `fluid validate`: the only way to get a hand-written quality rule into a published contract was to write an invalid contract. Optional and additive — a column without it exports exactly as it does today, with the rules forge derives from `required`, the primary-key tag and `validationRules`. Setting it REPLACES those derived rules for that column rather than adding to them, which is what makes an imported ODCS column round-trip byte-for-byte. The authority for an item's contents is ODCS v3.1.0 `$defs.DataQuality`, deliberately not re-declared here (a copy would drift from the vendored schema, and `fluid odcs validate` already checks an emitted document against it); the keys below are the common ones. Every rule should carry an `id`: it is optional in ODCS, but a DQ engine that labels its results by rule id rejects a contract whose rules have none. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].id` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Stable rule identifier, unique within this column's rules. The pattern is ODCS `$defs.StableId`. Rules forge derives itself are named `<column>-<metric>`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].type` | string | no | one of `text`, `library`, `sql`, `custom` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. ODCS quality check type. text = prose; library = one of ODCS's predefined metrics; sql = a query whose result is compared; custom = a named engine's own check. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.schema[].quality[].metric` | string | no | one of `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `invalidValues`, `duplicateValues`, `rowCount` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: library only. The five predefined metrics ODCS v3.1.0 defines; a name outside this list is not a library rule. |

| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality` | array of object | no | each item: min properties 1 |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. NEW in v0.7.6: Column-level data quality rules, in ODCS's own shape — the array that is written straight into `schema[].properties[].quality[]` of the exported ODCS v3.1.0 contract, and the array an imported ODCS column's rules are read back into, inline on the column rather than in the importer's pass-through bucket: the ODPS importer merges a resolved port's `contract` block into its output-port stub and discards the sub-import's root `extensions`, so rules left in that bucket were dropped outright by a FLUID → ODPS → FLUID cycle. The ODCS exporter has always replayed this key verbatim and always read it back on import, but `$defs.column` is `additionalProperties: false` and did not define it, so a column written the way the exporter supports was REFUSED by `fluid validate`: the only way to get a hand-written quality rule into a published contract was to write an invalid contract. Optional and additive — a column without it exports exactly as it does today, with the rules forge derives from `required`, the primary-key tag and `validationRules`. Setting it REPLACES those derived rules for that column rather than adding to them, which is what makes an imported ODCS column round-trip byte-for-byte. The authority for an item's contents is ODCS v3.1.0 `$defs.DataQuality`, deliberately not re-declared here (a copy would drift from the vendored schema, and `fluid odcs validate` already checks an emitted document against it); the keys below are the common ones. Every rule should carry an `id`: it is optional in ODCS, but a DQ engine that labels its results by rule id rejects a contract whose rules have none. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].id` | string | no | matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. Stable rule identifier, unique within this column's rules. The pattern is ODCS `$defs.StableId`. Rules forge derives itself are named `<column>-<metric>`. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].type` | string | no | one of `text`, `library`, `sql`, `custom` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. ODCS quality check type. text = prose; library = one of ODCS's predefined metrics; sql = a query whose result is compared; custom = a named engine's own check. |
| `builds[].properties.stream.key.schema[].quality[].metric` | string | no | one of `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `invalidValues`, `duplicateValues`, `rowCount` |  | Only when `pattern` is `embedded-logic`. type: library only. The five predefined metrics ODCS v3.1.0 defines; a name outside this list is not a library rule. |
